overlapping-shapes-and-dots.title: Overlapping Shapes and Dot Placement
overlapping-shapes-and-dots.methods: label every region of two or three overlapping shapes by which shapes contain it; record each dot's membership set (inside or outside each shape); find the region with the same membership set after the shapes move or change; handle two dots separately and check that both fit; tell a point on a boundary from a point inside; check every choice, since a region may be absent in some choices

more-figure-rules.title: More Figure Rules: Counts, Grids and Analogies
more-figure-rules.methods: relate a count in a figure to another count (sides to dots, sides to repeated shapes, including a difference of one); tell closed solids from open surfaces; one-of-each rules in rows and columns of a grid, with several blanks and two independent features; fit a missing pattern piece, including a rotated one, by continuing lines across its edges; visual analogies that swap fills or turn stripes; flat shape to solid relationships (square to cube, circle to sphere) and tracking openings; triangular prism nets with three rectangles, two triangles and a marked face
